newsitem.title: GERMANY: German M3 grows more strongly than expected.
newsitem.headline: German M3 grows more strongly than expected.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Thursday its main monetary policy indicator, German M3 money supply, grew strongly in January, which economists said further dampened any remaining hopes of a further interest rate cut.

The Bundesbank said M3 money supply grew at an annualised rate of 11.7 percent in January compared with its average level in the final quarter of 1996, above the top end of forecasts for a rate of just over eight percent.
But the Bundesbank itself warned that the data should be treated with caution as the statistical annualisation process tends to exaggerate developments in the early part of the year.
Economists polled by Reuters had forecast the annualised rate for growth in January M3 would lie between 4.5 and 8.2 percent compared with the average level in the fourth quarter of 1996.

To improve the comparison with December's 7.9 percent rate, the Bundesbank also released M3 data compared with the average level in the final quarter of 1995, which showed M3 growth grew at a stronger annualised rate of 8.6 percent in January.

The Bundesbank said January M3 growth was boosted by a strong statistical "overhang" at the end of 1996, by weak money capital formation -- investment in longer-term assets not included in M3 -- and by strong bank lending to the public sector.
